name: Fix a pod that won't start under hardening
objective: CKS › Minimize Microservice Vulnerabilities. Drill EVERY pod-hardening corner harder than the exam: runAsNonRoot/runAsUser, drop-ALL capabilities, readOnlyRootFilesystem, seccomp RuntimeDefault, privilege-escalation lockdown, a fully restricted-compliant pod, Pod Security Admission (enforce + audit/warn, pinned), and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod that won't start
questions.teach:
A pod that fails `runAsNonRoot` sits in a non-Ready state; `kubectl describe pod

` Events show `container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root` — the container set `runAsNonRoot: true` but no non-zero `runAsUser`, so the root image is rejected. Pin a non-zero `runAsUser`. **Gotcha:** fix the **securityContext** (add a non-zero `runAsUser`), not the image — a pod spec is immutable, so delete-and-recreate the pod with the fix.
questions.prompt:
Pod `broken-app` in `cks-podsec` **never becomes Ready** — `kubectl -n cks-podsec get pod broken-app` shows it isn't running. Diagnose the securityContext fault and fix it so the pod runs as a non-root UID.

Target: a pod named `broken-app` is `Running` with `runAsNonRoot=true` and a non-zero `runAsUser`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-podsec describe pod broken-app` → 'container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root'. It sets `runAsNonRoot: true` but no `runAsUser`. Delete it and recreate with `runAsUser: 1000` added.
questions.solution:
# describe shows: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root (0)
kubectl -n cks-podsec delete pod broken-app --force --grace-period=0
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: broken-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000
YAML

verification.description: broken-app Running with runAsNonRoot + non-zero runAsUser

questions.eli5:
A pod walks up to the door and the doorkeeper (the kubelet) checks its badge. The pod's rules say **"I promise not to run as root"** (`runAsNonRoot: true`) — but the image it's carrying (busybox) only knows how to log in as **root (user 0)**. So the pod has made a promise it can't keep. The doorkeeper refuses to let it start, and the pod just sits there never becoming Ready.

The way to *see* this is to ask the pod why it's unhappy: `kubectl describe pod broken-app` and read the **Events** at the bottom. You'll find the tell-tale line: *"container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root."* That sentence is the whole diagnosis — it promised non-root but has no non-zero user to actually be.

The fix is **not** to swap the image. It's to hand the pod a real, ordinary user number — `runAsUser: 1000` — so it can keep its "no root" promise. Now it logs in as user 1000 instead of root, and the doorkeeper is happy.

**Watch out:**

- **Fix the securityContext, not the image** — add a non-zero `runAsUser` (e.g. `1000`); don't go looking for a "non-root image."
- **A pod spec is largely immutable** — you can't just edit `runAsUser` into a live pod. **Delete and recreate** it with the fix.
- `runAsUser: 0` would NOT fix it — zero is still root. Use any non-zero UID.
- Read the **Events** in `kubectl describe pod` first — the error message names the exact problem for you.
- Keep `runAsNonRoot: true`; it's correct. The missing piece is only the non-zero UID that lets the promise hold.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: a pod that won't start under hardening — full rundown

### Mental model
This is the single most common `securityContext` failure: a container sets **`runAsNonRoot: true`** (a *gate* that forbids UID 0) but provides **no non-zero `runAsUser`**, and the image (busybox) defaults to **root (UID 0)**. The kubelet validates this at startup, sees the image would run as root, and refuses — the pod never becomes Ready. The method is: **describe → read the event → fix the securityContext → recreate**.

### Step 1 — observe
```bash
kubectl -n cks-podsec get pod broken-app
# STATUS is not Running (CreateContainerConfigError / not Ready)
```

### Step 2 — diagnose
```bash
kubectl -n cks-podsec describe pod broken-app | sed -n '/Events/,$p'
```
The signature event:
```
Error: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root
```
That line is the diagnosis: `runAsNonRoot: true` is set, but nothing pins a non-zero UID, and the image's default user is 0.

### Step 3 — fix
`runAsNonRoot` is **correct** and should stay — the missing piece is a non-zero `runAsUser`. Because most pod fields (including `securityContext`) are **immutable**, you cannot `kubectl edit` it into a running pod; delete and recreate.

```bash
kubectl -n cks-podsec delete pod broken-app --force --grace-period=0
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: broken-app, namespace: cks-podsec }
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      runAsUser: 1000        # the fix: a concrete non-zero UID
YAML
```

### Step 4 — confirm
```bash
kubectl -n cks-podsec get pod broken-app          # Running
kubectl -n cks-podsec exec broken-app -- id       # uid=1000 ...
```

### Related failure signatures (know the differences)
| Event / status | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root` | `runAsNonRoot: true`, no non-zero UID, root image | add `runAsUser: <non-zero>` |
| `Error: container's runAsUser breaks non-root policy (pod: ...)` | `runAsUser: 0` alongside `runAsNonRoot: true` | use a non-zero UID |
| `Read-only file system` → `CrashLoopBackOff` | `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` without writable mount | add `emptyDir` at the write path |
| PSA: `violates PodSecurity "restricted:..."` (rejected at create) | namespace enforces restricted; pod non-compliant | add the required restricted fields |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Fix the securityContext, not the image.** The intended answer is a non-zero `runAsUser`, not switching to a "rootless" image.
- **`runAsUser: 0` is not a fix** — zero is root; the gate still fails.
- **Pod specs are immutable** — you must **delete and recreate**, not edit, to change `runAsUser`. `--force --grace-period=0` speeds up deleting a stuck pod.
- **Always read `describe` Events first** — the message literally names the fault; don't guess.
- Keep `runAsNonRoot: true` — removing it would "fix" startup by *allowing root*, which defeats the hardening and is the wrong answer.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n cks-podsec describe pod broken-app | grep -i runasnonroot
kubectl -n cks-podsec delete pod broken-app --force --grace-period=0
# recreate with runAsNonRoot: true AND runAsUser: 1000
kubectl -n cks-podsec get pod broken-app          # Running
```
